title: Noetherian generic freeness for finite algebra-module pairs
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $B$ be a commutative $R$-algebra of finite type, meaning $B\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/J$ for some finite $n\geq0$ and an ideal $J$, and let $M$ be a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There exists $0\ne a\in R$ such that $M_a$ is a free $R_a$-module. Here $R_a=R[1/a]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $M_a$ is the localized module [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] of fractions $m/a^j$, with $m/a^j=m'/a^k$ if and only if $a^u(a^km-a^jm')=0$ for some $u\geq0$. Free means isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i\in I}R_a$ for some set $I$, not necessarily finite.

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation R[X_1,...,X_n] → B and restrict the module action along this surjection. Lifting coefficients in a finite B-generating set shows M is finite over this polynomial ring. It suffices to prove generic freeness for finite modules over polynomial algebras, simultaneously for every number of variables and all module universes.

source.place: exists_flatAway_of_mvPolynomial: polynomial filtration and stabilization argument, adapted from flatness to freeness by R8

proof.text: Induct on n. For n=0 the polynomial algebra is R, so M is finite and hence finitely presented over the Noetherian ring R. Over Frac(R) it is a vector space and therefore free. The finite-presentation free-localization theorem supplies a nonzero a in R for which M_a is free over R_a. This is the zero-prime case of the principal-neighborhood freeness lemma, using Mathlib Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers directly at nonZeroDivisors R.

source.place: exists_flatAway_of_mvPolynomial: polynomial filtration and stabilization argument, adapted from flatness to freeness by R8

proof.text: For the induction step, write A=T[x] with T isomorphic to R[X_1,...,X_n], and choose a finite A-generating set of M. Let N_i be the T-span of x^j m for j≤i and generators m. Each N_i is finite over T, N_i⊆N_(i+1), xN_i⊆N_(i+1), and their union is M: the union contains the generators and is stable under T and x, hence under A. The ring T is Noetherian by the polynomial-ring instance of finite-type permanence.

source.place: exists_flatAway_of_mvPolynomial: polynomial filtration and stabilization argument, adapted from flatness to freeness by R8

proof.text: Set Q_i=N_(i+1)/N_i. Multiplication by x^i induces a surjection Θ_i:Q_0→Q_i: modulo N_i only the degree i+1 generators remain, and they are x^i times degree-one generators. The kernels L_i of Θ_i form an increasing sequence, since xN_i⊆N_(i+1). The finite T-module Q_0 is Noetherian, so L_i stabilizes at some i_0; thus Q_i is isomorphic to Q_0/L_min(i,i_0). Apply the induction hypothesis to N_0 and to the finitely many modules Q_0/L_j for j≤i_0.

source.place: exists_flatAway_of_mvPolynomial: polynomial filtration and stabilization argument, adapted from flatness to freeness by R8

proof.text: Multiply the finitely many resulting nonzero localization elements. Further localization preserves freeness: use the tensor-product description of localized modules, base change of a free module, and cancellation of iterated base change. Hence N_0 and all Q_i become free at this single nonzero scalar a. Localization is exact, so the localized submodules P_i=(N_i)_a of M_a have P_(i+1)/P_i isomorphic to (Q_i)_a. Every fraction in M_a comes from some N_i, so the localized filtration remains exhaustive.

source.place: exists_flatAway_of_mvPolynomial: polynomial filtration and stabilization argument, adapted from flatness to freeness by R8

proof.text: For each i, projectivity of the free quotient P_(i+1)/P_i splits its quotient map. The range C_i of a section is free, disjoint from P_i, and P_i⊔C_i=P_(i+1). The family consisting of P_0 and the C_i is independent by induction on the maximum index in a finite set; its supremum is all of M_a by induction on the filtration and exhaustiveness. The direct-sum linear equivalence and the free-module instance on dependent finitely supported functions therefore show M_a is free. This argument allows arbitrary rank and also covers zero modules and zero algebras.
